narrative.overview:
A lab notebook is kept by the person using it. It holds what was run and what was checked, in order, and the next entry starts where the last one stopped. Each site in this family is such a notebook: opening it puts the owner back at the place they stopped, with the next thing to do in view. The record line in the page gutter and its "stopped here" mark are what a reader should remember.

The material is warm paper, warm ink and thin ruling, with five colors that each do one job, in a day and a night scheme. The colors are there to make reading easier, so they are dark enough to hold 7:1 as text and muted enough to be easy on the eyes. Pages are dense. Structure comes from hairlines and a shared left edge, not boxes, and nothing is there for decoration. The family rejects the template it shipped before: giant headline, tilted terminal, two buttons, stats row, card grid.

The family shares a language, not a layout. Each site's structure follows its own content, so copy these rules and never a sibling's page. `kit/v1/notebook.css` is the source of truth for values, and this file explains how to use them. It was recorded from two built surfaces: the project index in this repository and the C# design patterns course (course index, lesson, guide, quiz, playground).
keyCharacteristics: A record line in the gutter: solid green for what is done, dashed for what is not, with one blue tick where the owner stopped.
Five colors, each with one job, each holding 7:1 as text, and always a word beside them.
Two named schemes, 白天 and 晚上, with night composed rather than inverted.
Ruled rows instead of cards, with a wash only on short bands.
Pasted output between hairlines, with no window chrome.
Commands on their own line on a cyan wash, never broken inside a token.
Noto Sans SC at 400 and 600 for everything read, Cascadia Mono for code.
Chinese page titles that break between phrases, never inside a word.
Flat, flush-left, square-cornered, and the way back to the stopped place first.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Each of the five colors has the one job listed above, and none is used for emphasis, section accents or decoration. The one exception is a group's borrowed word, under the One Word Group Rule. Audit test: a page with no record has no tick, no 停在这里, no blue band and no solid green line.

rules.name: The Word Beside The Color Rule
rules.body: A color never carries a state alone: a written word always goes with it, and records and verdicts keep their line form too. A correct quiz answer gets a 2px solid green rule and 正确, a wrong one gets a 1px dashed red rule and 你的选择, and a locked step gets a dashed box. Every text color holds 7:1 on paper, on the sheet and on every wash in both schemes, with the lowest at 7.17:1 by day and 7.15:1 at night, and `tests/home.mjs` enforces it. Hue is less reliable than contrast. Measured as OKLab distance times 100, the closest pairs for normal vision are green and cyan by day at 10.0 and blue and purple at night at 7.8. Under simulated deuteranopia, blue and purple come within 3.9 by day and cyan and purple within 2.4 at night. Under simulated protanopia, blue and purple come within 3.8 by day and 2.4 at night. Audit test: in grayscale the page still says what is done.

rules.name: The Short Band Rule
rules.body: Red, green, cyan and blue each have a wash, and a wash is for short bands only: the resume band, a stopped row in a register, command rows, search hits, quiz option verdicts, the storage warning and a pressed problem chip. Tall panels mark the stopped place with a blue heading, not a fill. On the index the resume band fills, so the stopped row below it does not fill again. The quiz's teaching text stays on plain paper with only a colored rule and verdict. Reading text on a wash stays ink, at 10.0:1 or better in both schemes. A wash is 1.07:1 to 1.25:1 against paper, so it is never the only sign of anything. The resume band and quiz verdicts reach past the text edge by their own padding, so their words stay on the shared left edge.

rules.name: The Stands Off The Paper Rule
rules.body: A color earns its place only if it differs from the paper in hue as well as in lightness. Orange and yellow failed this on warm paper even at 7:1, and the owner asked for colors close to the background to go, so they are not in the kit. Don't bring them back for emphasis, warnings or categories, and judge a new color on the page, not only by its contrast number.

rules.name: The One Word Group Rule
rules.body: A site's own groups borrow a hue through `data-hue` for one word only: the topic on an index row, the category word on a pattern row and in its dialog, and a filter button, with any count it shows. Pattern numbers stay soft, and nothing else in the row takes the hue. The index has 工程 purple, 算法 cyan, 前端 green and AI blue. The course has 创建型 blue, 结构型 purple and 行为型 cyan. These overlap the colors' jobs. Green on 前端 overlaps done, and blue on AI and 创建型 overlaps links. A reviewer flagged this kind of overlap, and it was kept deliberately, because the owner asked for color and a gray category would be worse. This is an accepted trade-off, not an accident, so don't correct it. Purple on 工程 and 结构型 and cyan on 算法 and 行为型 overlap code and commands in the same way. A lesson's 运行并追踪 and 何时避免 headings use the same attribute to carry their job color, not a group.

rules.name: The Composed Night Rule
rules.body: The two schemes are named 白天 and 晚上, and night is composed, not inverted: warm black paper and warm ink, not blue-black and near white. `--nb-rule-bold` softens heavy rules at night (by day it equals ink), `--nb-fill` is a deeper blue with warm paper text, and each wash keeps its own hue on the dark paper. Night tokens live in `@media screen`, so printing is always in day colors.

rules.name: The Achromatic Field Rule
rules.body: Text fields carry no color of their own: transparent fill, Strong Ruling outline and Soft Ink placeholder. Only the focus ring and the caret are blue.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Everything but code is set in Noto Sans SC at 400 or 600, the two weights in the shared font files, so a page never changes voice between its head and its text. The owner rejected a Noto Serif SC head over a Microsoft YaHei body on 2026-11-02 as awkward: two voices met in one row, YaHei draws quotation marks narrow, and Segoe UI digits sat lighter than YaHei bold in the same heading. `theme.js` adds `/kit/v1/fonts.css` on the production host only, so a local preview uses an installed Noto Sans SC or falls back to the system face.

rules.name: The Whole Phrase Rule
rules.body: Page titles use `word-break: keep-all` with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. In Chinese this limits breaks to spaces and punctuation, so 设计模式 stays whole, and `anywhere` remains as the emergency exit that stops a long title overflowing a phone. The kit sets this on every first-level heading. Add the same pair to anything else that shows a course or lesson title, such as the continue link. Write titles with natural break points (a space, `：`, `·`), because a long run with none gets cut wherever the emergency break lands.

rules.name: The No Balance Rule
rules.body: Don't use `text-wrap: balance` on Chinese text. It was tried on headings and removed because it split 下单 in the middle of a word on the OnlineStore guide title: it looks for equal line lengths, and Chinese offers it a break between any two characters, with no word boundaries to respect. `text-wrap: pretty` stays on headings and paragraphs for last-line orphans, but it does not stop mid-word splits either, which is why the Whole Phrase Rule exists.

rules.name: The Chinese Reading Rule
rules.body: Every page sets `lang="zh-CN"` and lets the kit's body settings reach the text: `line-break: strict` for line-start and line-end punctuation, `text-spacing-trim: trim-start` so an opening `（` at the start of a line does not look indented, `text-autospace: normal` for spacing between Chinese and Latin, and line height 1.75. An engine's stylesheet must not override them.

rules.name: The Narrow Dot Rule
rules.body: Noto Sans SC draws `·` full width, which opens wide gaps in labels written as `a · b`. The kit's `NB Dot` face at the front of the sans stack takes that one character from a Latin face, using `unicode-range`. Keep that face first if an engine's font variable is replaced.

rules.name: The Literal Code Rule
rules.body: Code uses Cascadia Mono, not Cascadia Code, with ligatures off, so `--` and `->` read exactly as they are typed. Put it first in the stack, because a `font:` shorthand resets the kit's ligature setting.

rules.name: The Flush Left Rule
rules.body: All text is left-aligned on one left edge, and nothing is centered: no centered headings, copy blocks or empty states. Only secondary things sit at the far edge: the head nav and scheme control, the search box, the state column, the next link. The one centered thing is the capped page block in a window wider than 72rem.

rules.name: The Continue First Rule
rules.body: The way back to the stopped place is the first action on a site's opening screen, and nothing above it pitches the site. On the index it is a row at the top left, under 200px from the top of the window. On a course it sits directly under the title, beside the thing to run. With no record yet, it offers the first step or says plainly that there is no record.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. If something needs separating, rule a line.

rules.name: The Square Box Rule
rules.body: Anything drawn as a box has 2px corners or none: controls, dialogs and the favicon tile at 2px, pasted output, wash bands, toasts and rows at none. Nothing is a pill. Radio buttons stay native and round.

rules.name: The Solid And Dashed Rule
rules.body: In the record line, solid green means done and dashed means not done, so gaps in the work read as breaks in the line. Solid is never drawn for progress that is not on record, and dashed is never used as decoration.

rules.name: The Ruled Row Rule
rules.body: Lists and grouped content are rows between hairlines. No row or panel gets a radius or a shadow. The only rows that fill are short ones, under the Short Band Rule: the stopped row of a register on the blue wash, and a quiz option once it has its verdict.

rules.name: The No Window Chrome Rule
rules.body: Output has hairlines above and below on the Pasted Sheet, and that is all: no title bar, traffic lights, tab strip, tilt, shadow or dark window on a light page.

rules.name: The Whole Token Rule
rules.body: A command never wraps and never breaks inside a token. It sits on its own line on the cyan wash with `white-space: pre`, `overflow-x: auto` and `min-width: 0`, and a long one scrolls sideways in its own box, even if that cuts it off at the edge of a phone. Anything meant to be copied gets a command row, and inline code is for short names.

dos: **Do** take every color from the kit's tokens and let `data-theme` switch them.
**Do** give each of the five colors its one job, and check any new use against the list.
**Do** give every list of work a record line: solid green for what is done, dashed for what is not, with one blue tick at the stopped place.
**Do** check a page with no record on it. It should show no tick, no 停在这里, no blue band and no solid green line.
**Do** build lists as ruled rows, with each site choosing its own columns from its own content.
**Do** keep a wash to a short band, and mark the stopped place in a tall panel with a blue heading.
**Do** paste real output on the sheet between 1px hairlines.
**Do** give each command its own line on the cyan wash with `white-space: pre` and `overflow-x: auto`.
**Do** keep `word-break: keep-all` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on page titles, and write those titles with natural break points.
**Do** set `lang="zh-CN"` and keep `line-break: strict`, `text-spacing-trim: trim-start` and `text-autospace: normal` reaching the text.
**Do** pair every colored state with a written word, and keep the line form in records and verdicts.
**Do** check a new color value against `tests/home.mjs`, which holds every text color to 7:1 on paper, sheet and every wash in both schemes.
**Do** put the continue link first on a site's opening screen.
**Do** carry over the kit's reduced-motion and forced-colors handling when an engine replaces a component.
**Do** show only counts that come from the repository or the owner's own record.
donts: **Don't** use a color outside its job, for emphasis or as an accent. A group's borrowed word is the one exception, and an accepted one.
**Don't** add a sixth color, bring back orange or yellow, or give one of the five a second job.
**Don't** let a color carry a state without a word.
**Don't** turn anything green for work that is only started.
**Don't** fill a tall panel or teaching text with a wash, or fill the stopped row when a band above it already fills.
**Don't** use red in code.
**Don't** make night by inverting day.
**Don't** draw a dashed line as decoration, or a solid record line for work that is not on record.
**Don't** use cards: no filled tiles, rounded panels or grids of boxes.
**Don't** draw a terminal: no title bar, traffic lights, tab strip, tilt or shadow around output.
**Don't** use `pre-wrap` or `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on commands.
**Don't** use `text-wrap: balance` on Chinese text.
**Don't** remove `keep-all` from a page title because it breaks badly; shorten the title or give it a break point.
**Don't** center headings, copy or empty states.
**Don't** open a site with the old template: giant headline, tilted terminal, two buttons, stats row, card grid.
**Don't** use shadows, blur or pill shapes.
**Don't** add a serif or a second Chinese family, or use any weight but 400 and 600.
**Don't** use uppercase, letter-spacing or justified text.
**Don't** add icons. Controls are words, and the only drawn marks are the record line, the tick and the check.
**Don't** put a small label above a title. Keys and categories get their own column or row.
**Don't** edit a site's copy of the kit, or change a published kit version.
**Don't** copy a sibling site's page structure. The family shares rules, not a template.
